subject: SprintPay — operational impact assessment and next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sprintpay.net>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: SprintPay — operational impact assessment and next steps

Hi Alex — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can line up the right team for the dedicated-capacity sizing call:

What we heard (summary)
- Primary use: real-time invoice classification + conversational query for customer support.
- Peak concurrency: ~200–300 inference requests/sec (expected burst patterns around 11:00–13:00 PT).
- SLO target: 99th percentile generation latency <200ms for short responses (<=128 tokens); toggle longer-tail batch paths for async reports.
- Average token consumption (estimate): ~25 tokens/request; peak sustained tokens/day ~180M.

Why a dedicated sizing call
- We want to validate request distribution, KV cache patterns, and exact latency SLOs so the Dedicated pool matches your cost/latency goals. This is not a demo; it’s a technical intake for capacity planning.

Proposed next steps (pick one)
1) Tue 2028-05-16 10:00–11:00 PT — dedicated sizing call (preferred; allows east/west follow-up)
2) Wed 2028-05-17 14:00–15:00 PT — alternate slot

On that call we’ll bring: serving runtime lead + solutions engineer (Marcus) and a short checklist we’ll run through. Action items for you before the call:
- Share a 48–72h sample of request logs or aggregated QPS histograms (no PII).
- Confirm true 99% SLO target (200ms?) and whether async fallbacks are acceptable for heavier prompts.

Attached: SprintPay_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx — a compact intake table to fill where you have rough numbers. Also attached a draft demo agenda (redwood_demo_agenda.pdf) in case you want a demo immediately after sizing (we can stack both).

If those slots don’t work, tell me two windows that do and I’ll coordinate. Thanks — appreciate the time today.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0132 | (e) tessa@redwood.com

(Attachment: SprintPay_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx)
(Attachment: redwood_demo_agenda.pdf)

Thanks Tessa — super clear, appreciate the recap.

Both slots look possible; we’d prefer Tue 2028-05-16 10:00–11:00 PT. I’ll try to get our infra lead (Sara Li) on the call too.

A couple of notes:
- Confirming the 99th target at 200ms for short responses — anything above that degrades our UX.
- We’ll try to export a 72h sampling of the request histogram (an aggregated view) and I’ll drop it into the intake spreadsheet.
- Procurement: procurement@sprintpay.net — I’ll CC them into a follow-up for commercial/contract prep (they’ll want an NDA before detailed logs if needed).

Tessa / Alex — logging fields checklist below (I’ll paste this into the Drive doc as well):
- timestamp (UTC), endpoint, latency_ms (total), model_variant, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, success_flag, error_code (if any), request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, cache_hit (bool).
- Aggregates: 1m/5m QPS buckets, p50/p95/p99 latencies per endpoint, burst length distribution (how long bursts >X QPS last).

I’ll build a one-pager to share before the call; can we ask SprintPay to populate the intake sheet with peak-hour examples + 24h rolling window? That will let us sketch a GPU pool options matrix before the meeting.

Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
